cards.text: The writer of this letter just warned his readers to test every spirit, because false prophets are out there (1 John 4:1). Now he switches gears, like a manager who wraps up the fire drill speech and goes, 'Okay, who wants cookies?' He says, 'Beloved, let us love one another, because love comes from God.'

cards.question: The writer says love comes from God. What does he say about everyone who loves?

answers.text: They have been born of God and know God
They have earned a place with God
They have been chosen to lead others

cards.text: Born of God and knowing God: that's a family resemblance, friend, like every cookie off the same stamp coming out with the same FACE. So what about somebody who doesn't love?

cards.question: The writer says someone who doesn't love can still know God just fine. True or false?

cards.text: Whoever doesn't love doesn't know God, and he gives the reason: 'God is love.'

cards.question: The writer says God's love was revealed among us. How did God show it?

answers.text: He sent His one and only Son into the world
He sent a prophet into every single nation
He wrote His law on two tablets of stone

cards.text: God sent His Son so that we might live through Him. Then the writer says what love consists in, and friend, I've spent YEARS trying to explain the perfect cookie, and I still just point at the oven.

cards.question: So what does the writer say love consists in?

answers.text: Not that we loved God but that He loved us
Not that we obeyed God but that we kept trying
Not that we feared God but that we served Him

cards.question: The writer says God sent His Son as the atoning sacrifice for our ___.

cards.text: Calling them 'Beloved' again, he brings it home: if God so loved us, we also ought to love one another. You get loved like THAT, friend, you don't hide it like a batch of cookies in the back of the cupboard.
Then he says it straight: no one has ever seen God.

cards.question: No one has ever seen God. But what does the writer say happens if we love one another?

answers.text: God remains in us and His love is perfected in us
We will see God face to face in this life
We will never again be tempted to sin

cards.text: Next he tackles a big one: how do we KNOW we remain in God, and He in us? Friend, I spent years in a drawer stuffed with old receipts, and not ONE of them could've proved that.

cards.question: How does the writer say we know we remain in God and He in us?

answers.text: He has given us of His Spirit
We have never once doubted Him
We were raised in a godly home

cards.text: Then he says we have seen it and we testify: the Father sent His Son to be the Savior of the world. That's not a rumor from somebody's group chat, friend, that's EYEWITNESSES.

cards.question: The writer says that if anyone confesses that Jesus is the Son of God, God abides in him, and he in God. True or false?

cards.text: He says we have come to know and believe the love God has for us, and then comes that line again: God is love. Friend, I'd frame that one and hang it right over my ovens.

cards.question: The writer says whoever abides in ___ abides in God, and God in him.

cards.text: He says love has been perfected among us, and that reaches all the way to the day of judgment.

cards.question: The writer says love is perfected among us so that we may have ___ on the day of judgment.
What reason does the writer give for that confidence on the day of judgment?

answers.text: In this world we are just like Him
In this world we have done no wrong
In this world we have kept His law

cards.text: Then he says there is no fear in love. Friend, I jump every single time my oven timer goes off, so I'm taking NOTES.

cards.question: What does the writer say perfect love does with fear?
The writer gives a reason perfect love drives out fear: fear involves punishment. True or false?

cards.text: He says the one who fears has not been perfected in love. Then he says it plain: 'We love because He first loved us.'
Now somebody says, 'I love God,' but hates his brother. That's like a guy who posts all day about how much he LOVES his neighborhood, then won't even wave at the man next door.

cards.question: What does the writer call someone who says he loves God but hates his brother?
The writer says a person can love God, whom he hasn't seen, without loving his brother, whom he has seen. True or false?
The writer says whoever loves God must love his brother as well. What does he call that?
